# The Most Used IDE

You just met several real IDEs. This lesson answers a simple question: which one do most developers actually reach for, and why did it win out over the others?

## The most used IDE today

In wide surveys of professional developers, like the well known Stack Overflow Developer Survey, one tool has come out on top for several years in a row: **Visual Studio Code**, often just called VS Code, made by Microsoft.

<img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," alt="Illustration of a Visual Studio Code style editor window with a blue title bar" width="240" height="140">

## Why it became the most used

No single reason explains it. It is really a combination of smaller advantages that add up.

1. **It is free.** Anyone can download and use it, with no cost and no license to buy, unlike some older professional IDEs.
2. **It works everywhere.** The same program runs on Windows, Mac, and Linux, so it fits almost any developer's setup.
3. **It is fast and light.** It starts up quickly and stays responsive, even though it can still do a lot, unlike some heavier, all-in-one IDEs that can feel slow.
4. **It has a huge library of extensions.** Support for nearly any language, from Python to JavaScript to many others, can be added with a couple of clicks, so one editor can cover almost every project a developer works on.
5. **It has a large, active community.** Because so many developers already use it, there are enormous amounts of free tutorials, guides, and shared extensions, which makes learning it, and getting help with it, much easier.
6. **It is actively maintained.** Microsoft ships small updates roughly every month, steadily improving it year after year instead of leaving it to go stale.

Put together, this is why so many developers, from complete beginners to experienced professionals, tend to land on the same tool.

## Its environment, a closer look

- A **sidebar** on the left switches between the file explorer, search, and other panels.
- An **extensions marketplace**, built right in, is where you browse and install add-ons for new languages or tools.
- A **command palette**, opened with a keyboard shortcut, lets you search for and run almost any action by typing its name, instead of hunting through menus.
- A **built-in terminal** lets you type commands directly to your computer, without switching to a separate program.
- **Split editing** lets you view and edit two files side by side.

## What you learned

- Visual Studio Code is currently the most used IDE among developers, according to wide surveys.
- Its popularity comes from being free, fast, cross-platform, and backed by a huge library of extensions and an active community.
- Its environment includes a sidebar, a built-in extensions marketplace, a command palette, a built-in terminal, and split editing.

That wraps up this introduction to IDEs. From here, it is time to start writing real code, beginning with HTML.
